name: Gold & Commodity Return Correlations
description: Analyzes return correlations between Gold futures (GC), SPY, and a broad commodity basket (SI, CL, NG, HG, ZW, ZC, ZS). Computes daily, weekly, and monthly returns. Displays pairwise correlation heatmaps for each return timeframe, a cross-sectional summary table of each asset's correlation with GC and SPY, and a rolling 90-day correlation timeseries between GC and every other asset.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Gold & Commodity Return Correlations
# Universe: GC, SI, CL, NG, HG, ZW, ZC, ZS futures + SPY (reference)
# Outputs:
#   1. Pairwise correlation heatmaps — daily, weekly, monthly returns
#   2. Cross-sectional summary table — correlation with GC and SPY (rolling 90d)
#   3. Rolling 90-day correlation timeseries — each asset vs GC
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. MARKET DATA — Futures (per-asset via universe)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

src = market_data_source(timeframe=1D)()

cont = futures_continuation(
    timeframe=1D,
    s_rollover_method=RolloverType.FirstOfMonth,
    s_adjustment_method=AdjustmentType.BackwardPanamaCanal
)(src.o, src.h, src.l, src.c, src.v, src.oi, src.s)

close = cont.c

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. SPY — Cross-sectional reference
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

spy_src = reference_stocks(ticker='SPY')()
close_spy = spy_src.c

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. RETURNS — Daily (1d), Weekly (~5d), Monthly (~21d)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Per-asset (futures)
ret_daily   = returns(period=1)(close)
ret_weekly  = returns(period=5)(close)
ret_monthly = returns(period=21)(close)

# SPY reference returns
ret_spy_daily   = returns(period=1)(close_spy)
ret_spy_weekly  = returns(period=5)(close_spy)
ret_spy_monthly = returns(period=21)(close_spy)

# =============================================================================
# 4. CORRELATION HEATMAPS — cs_heatmap(mode=correlation) per timeframe
# =============================================================================
# cs_heatmap in correlation mode computes the full NxN pairwise matrix
# across all assets feeding the same input slot.
# SPY is included via reference_stocks and fed alongside futures returns.
# Because cs_heatmap is a cross-sectional reporter (isCrossSectional=false but
# executes across universe), we feed the per-asset return series directly.

cs_heatmap(
    mode=HeatmapMode.correlation,
    title="Daily Return Correlation Matrix",
    category="1. Correlation Heatmaps",
    color_axis_min=-1.0,
    color_axis_max=1.0,
    min_color=Color.Blue,
    max_color=Color.Red,
    show_data_labels=True,
    data_label_format="{point.value:.2f}",
    max_assets=20
)(ret_daily)

cs_heatmap(
    mode=HeatmapMode.correlation,
    title="Weekly Return Correlation Matrix (~5-day)",
    category="1. Correlation Heatmaps",
    color_axis_min=-1.0,
    color_axis_max=1.0,
    min_color=Color.Blue,
    max_color=Color.Red,
    show_data_labels=True,
    data_label_format="{point.value:.2f}",
    max_assets=20
)(ret_weekly)

cs_heatmap(
    mode=HeatmapMode.correlation,
    title="Monthly Return Correlation Matrix (~21-day)",
    category="1. Correlation Heatmaps",
    color_axis_min=-1.0,
    color_axis_max=1.0,
    min_color=Color.Blue,
    max_color=Color.Red,
    show_data_labels=True,
    data_label_format="{point.value:.2f}",
    max_assets=20
)(ret_monthly)

# =============================================================================
# 5. ROLLING 90-DAY CORRELATIONS vs GC and vs SPY
# =============================================================================
# GC is a primary asset — its returns are available per-asset via the universe.
# We use reference_stocks for SPY (cross-sectional).
# For the rolling_corr vs GC: we use a cross-sectional reference stock trick —
# load GC as a reference stock so its return series is available universally.

gc_ref = reference_stocks(ticker='GC=F')()
close_gc_ref = gc_ref.c
ret_gc_ref_daily = returns(period=1)(close_gc_ref)

# Rolling 90-day correlation: each asset's daily return vs GC and vs SPY
corr_vs_gc  = rolling_corr(window=90, window_type=WindowType.rolling, method=CorrelationMethod.pearson)(x=ret_gc_ref_daily, y=ret_daily)
corr_vs_spy = rolling_corr(window=90, window_type=WindowType.rolling, method=CorrelationMethod.pearson)(x=ret_spy_daily,   y=ret_daily)

# =============================================================================
# 6. CROSS-SECTIONAL SUMMARY TABLE
#    Rows = each asset | Columns = Corr vs GC (90d), Corr vs SPY (90d)
# =============================================================================

cs_summary_table(
    title="90-Day Rolling Correlation with GC and SPY (Latest)",
    category="2. Correlation Summary",
    agg=AggregationType.Last,
    schema=TableReportSchema(columns=[
        ColumnSpec(title="Corr vs GC (90d)",  type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=3),
        ColumnSpec(title="Corr vs SPY (90d)", type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=3)
    ])
)(corr_vs_gc, corr_vs_spy)

# =============================================================================
# 7. ROLLING 90-DAY CORRELATION TIMESERIES — Each Asset vs GC
# =============================================================================
# timeseries_lines renders per-asset in TV chart view.
# We use xy_lines (dashboard) with index() as x-axis for a dashboard chart.

bar_idx = index()()

xy_lines(
    title="Rolling 90-Day Correlation vs GC",
    category="3. Rolling Correlation vs GC",
    x_axis_label="Date",
    y_axis_label="Pearson Correlation",
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name="vs GC (90d)", color=Color.Gold)
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0,    color=Color.Gray,  dash_style=DashStyle.Dash,  title="Zero"),
        ReferenceLine(value=0.5,  color=Color.Green, dash_style=DashStyle.Dot,   title="+0.50"),
        ReferenceLine(value=-0.5, color=Color.Red,   dash_style=DashStyle.Dot,   title="-0.50")
    ])
)(bar_idx, corr_vs_gc)

# Rolling 90-day SPY correlation timeseries (per-asset)
xy_lines(
    title="Rolling 90-Day Correlation vs SPY",
    category="3. Rolling Correlation vs GC",
    x_axis_label="Date",
    y_axis_label="Pearson Correlation",
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name="vs SPY (90d)", color=Color.Sky)
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0,    color=Color.Gray,  dash_style=DashStyle.Dash,  title="Zero"),
        ReferenceLine(value=0.5,  color=Color.Green, dash_style=DashStyle.Dot,   title="+0.50"),
        ReferenceLine(value=-0.5, color=Color.Red,   dash_style=DashStyle.Dot,   title="-0.50")
    ])
)(bar_idx, corr_vs_spy)
